questions.text: Who must start helping if I can't ask?
Do I count without papers, citizenship or a family?
What does the record accept as evidence — and what can a temporary name not prove?
What am I owed — and do I have to earn it?
Does a receipt prove I was fed?
What if there is genuinely not enough — and who owes when the ordinary route fails?
What does nobody need permission for?
Can a wage or a supplement be a condition on essentials?
Can money or contribution buy standing?
Is the route the same for everyone?
Do ecological limits and animals have claims of their own?
Who may hold a role in my life?
Does arriving put a price on personhood?
Does answerability end when an official leaves office?
How is public power built and divided?
Can a conviction take my vote?
What may be kept about me — and reused?
Does a crisis suspend the republic?
How do I get heard, and what can a court order?
Can a future majority remove the floor?
Am I protected after exposing authority?
Whose findings count when authority is absent, forged or stale?
Can a credibility finding erase what I have done?
Can they hold me — and what stays mine?
Is a recorded placement an actual place?
What happens when the system notices it broke?

terms.name: entry
terms.definition: A supplied report, such as a birth, judgment or receipt.

terms.name: record
terms.definition: The entries supplied for the rules to read. Its vocabulary can be restricted while its contents are false, incomplete or stale.

terms.name: rule
terms.definition: A route from specified premises to a conclusion. It does not verify the premises for itself.

terms.name: derived
terms.definition: Established from the exact rules and supplied record being checked. It does not mean observed in the world.

terms.name: person
terms.definition: The status from which the floor follows. A birth or encounter can establish it; custody and release supply independent backstops.

terms.name: standing
terms.definition: The universal status every person holds. It is neither a rank nor permission to act on someone.

terms.name: floor
terms.definition: What every person is owed without conditions of employment, registration, belonging, payment or approved behaviour.

terms.name: delivery
terms.definition: The protected condition reaching a person. A debt, payment or institutional output is not enough to establish it.

terms.name: receipt
terms.definition: A report of delivery. The ordinary receipt route needs matching independent evidence before delivery can be concluded.

terms.name: shield
terms.definition: Protection against conviction-based imprisonment following an exposure of authority, while no effective deceit finding applies to that exposure.

terms.name: voiding
terms.definition: An effective credibility finding that prevents a new adverse signature from qualifying. It leaves the floor intact.

terms.name: placement
terms.definition: Reviewed authority for a named place of confinement. It does not establish that anyone was moved there or received shelter.

terms.name: breach marker
terms.definition: A conclusion naming a defect in the supplied record. It does not itself investigate, correct, compensate or release anyone.

terms.name: democratic corridor
terms.definition: The range of public choices within constitutional invariants and protected freedoms, with review and peaceful change.
